newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC has no plans for big N. America step.
newsitem.headline: SBC has no plans for big N. America step.

text.p: Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) chief executive Marcel Ospel said the company had no plans for a major investment banking acquisition in North America, but was on the lookout for possible deals to expand private banking.
Asked in the April edition of Euromoney magazine about rumours SBC was about to do something big in North America, Ospel said he was unaware of such talk.

"I can confirm there are no such plans. The market for U.S. investment banks is vastly overpriced. The ongoing dilution of the regulatory environment will change the landscape for investment and private banking in North America," he said.

"We want to know more about what will happen before we consider anything. However, if there was an opportunity here and there -- in particular to buy a franchise or expertise by acquiring a small boutique -- we'd consider it."
Banking analysts have stated in the past that a North American acquisition would make sense for SBC to round out its global operations.
Ospel dismissed the idea of buying a second-tier U.S. investment bank.

"Some players in the second and third brackets have been on the market for a while. If we'd intended to buy one, we'd have moved a few years ago," he said, adding the approach of hiring away top people did not seem likely to be successful.
Ospel ruled out acquisitions "at this juncture" for asset management division SBC Brinson, but said SBC was still on the lookout for acquisitions in private banking.

"We'll continue to buy franchises, as we did when we bought businesses from Chase Manhattan and Standard Chartered during 1996. In some markets you can also expect us to buy smaller boutique-type private banks with strong franchise value."
He said the group was on track to hit its return on equity (ROE) target of 15 percent by 1999.

"Warburg is well above that target after tax and the group reached its ROE goals for 1996. We further expect to hit the targeted result for 1997. Last year ROE after tax was 10.1 percent. We expect it to be a little north of 12 percent this year, and then 15 percent by 1999," he said.
Ospel played down the chances that two of Switzerland's big three banks could merge.

"I think bank mega-mergers are more likely to happen in Europe outside Switzerland, once EMU (economic and monetary union) harmonises financial markets. If you look around, you see some banks positioning themselves for that already," he said.
"All the big three banks in Switzerland seem to be on a downsizing track which will keep us busy for a while."
Ospel said SBC had no plans to boost cooperation with Zurich Insurance.
"We are close in terms of leveraging each other's franchise domestically and selling each other's products, but we have no joint operations and don't have any intention of starting any."
